title: Technology Sector Update for 09/04/2018: AMD,INTC,APPF,WIT,JD

Technology stocks pared some of their prior losses this afternoon, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 Tuesday losing over 0.4% in value although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was nearly 0.7% higher in late trade.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares climbed to a 12-year high on Tuesday, rising over 11% to touch its best price since June 2006 at $28.06 a share after two analysts at separate brokerages raised their respective price targets for the company's stock to $30 a share. Jefferies analyst Mark Lipacis increased his price target by $8 from $22 previously while Matthew Ramsay at Cowen & Co analyst added $5 to his prior $25 target and also maintained his Outperform rating, with CNBC reporting they believe the chipmaker has developed a significant edge in technology over rival Intel ( INTC ).
In other sector news:
(+) AppFolio ( APPF ) was trading near its session high Tuesday, rising almost 3%, after the business software company Tuesday said it has acquired WegoWise, which has developed cloud-based analytics software designed to assist building owners better manage their spending on utilities. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. AppFolio said the acquisition will become a building block for an utility management service it expects to offer to its real estate customers.
(+) Wipro ( WIT ) rose 3% at one point on Tuesday after saying it received a contract to provide technology assistance to human resources and employee benefits administrator Alight Solutions expected to generate between $1.5 billion to $1.6 billion over its 10-year term, representing Wipro's largest contract win yet.
-JD.com ( JD ) slumped as much as 7% on Tuesday after CEO Liu Qiangdong was arrested Friday in Minneapolis and later released while police investigate allegations of criminal sexual conduct. In a statement issued Monday by his attorney, Liu denied all accusations of misconduct, adding he doesn't expect any charges will be filed. The company earlier Tuesday said Liu was back at work in China. The Financial Times reported the incident involves a University of Minnesota student.
